items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:1
items.html:
The Sefirot of Akudim, comprising six chapters in which six principal matters are explained: 1. the matter of couplings by striking and clashes. 2. the matter of reflected light. 3. the matter of the records. 4. the matter of the vessels. 5. the matter of the screen. 6. the matter of direct light.

Since the ARI’s words here are all fundamental, and all the foundations of the wisdom are built upon them, and there is not one small matter in all the worlds ABYA that does not contain within it, in general and in particular, outcomes of all the matters brought here in the ten Sefirot of Akudim — and not only that, but from every slight change and small novelty here there branch out in the Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] of ABYA many and very deep matters. For it is known that all the forces and novel forms that are in the upper ones must be found in every one lower than them, and not even a small detail is lacking; and this holds throughout the whole continuation of the cascading of the Partzufim and the worlds until the end of Assiya, and all the more so here, where we are still engaged with the first line, which is drawn from Ein Sof [infinity] to the place of the restriction, which is the first Partzuf of Adam Kadmon. Therefore every single word here is a pearl precious beyond all value, which must be understood in its full breadth and in its true definition, and repeated and remembered throughout the whole continuation of the wisdom.
And therefore I have come to arrange here the principal matters brought in this part, in an order that assists the memory, and also to discern in each matter the essential discernments that the ARI brings here, and to define every thing as far as possible, so that the student may guard himself against taking anything outside its faithful definition; for a slight error in these places halts the understanding entirely in the continuation of the wisdom.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:2
items.html:
Chapter 1
Five kinds of couplings by striking and clashes
Five kinds of couplings by striking and clashes we find here in the ARI’s words, in the first expansion of AK, which are:
1 Called the first look, which is a coupling by striking of the upper light on the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut, which is for the phase of the vessels of the Rosh [head]. (as above in Part 3, Chapter 12, Item 4).
2 Is the striking and clash of the inner light and the surrounding light in one another as they emerge outside the Peh [mouth] of AK, which the ARI brings here (Chapter 1, Item 3).
3, Called the second look, which is a coupling by striking of the upper light on the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut, which is to make vessels for the Guf [body]. (brought in Part 3, Chapter 12, Item 5, and in Etz Chaim, Gate 4, Chapter 3).
4, The striking and clash of the record and the descending reflected light in one another. (brought here in Chapter 3, Item 9).
5, The clash of the light of Malchut with the descending reflected light. (brought here in Chapter 4, Item 3).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:3
items.html:
The first coupling by striking makes only roots of vessels; the second — the vessel and the light are mixed; the third makes complete vessels
Now the root of them all is the coupling that is called the first look, from which is drawn all the light that is in the Partzuf, and its matter has already been well explained in the ARI’s words (in Part 3, Chapter 1, Item 1, and Chapter 12, Items 2 and 3). Indeed, it suffices only to bring out roots of vessels, which is called a phase of clothing in potential and not actually in practice. For the reflected light here clothes from below upwards, the meaning of which is a phase of resistance to clothing in the coarseness of the vessel; and therefore the ten Sefirot that are in the Rosh [head] are called by the name Ein Sof [infinity], or Keter [crown], as the ARI writes (ibid., Part 3, Chapter 6, Item 7), see there. And not only that, but even afterwards, when the ten Sefirot expanded from the Malchut of the Rosh downwards into the Guf [body] until the Tabur, there is still no phase of vessels there discernible in themselves; rather the light and the vessels are as though mixed together, as the ARI writes here (Chapter 6, Item 1), see there. And the principal revelation of the existence of the vessels begins from the second look, which is made upon the screen that is in the vessel of Malchut at the time of refinement, that is, the four levels that emerge in the degrees of its refinement.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:4
items.html:
The third coupling by striking is made by the surrounding light and the inner light, in that the surrounding light refines the screen and the upper light couples by striking upon the screen in the degrees of its refinement and brings out four levels, HB TM
And the matter of this refinement is made by the striking of the inner light and the surrounding light in one another, as the ARI writes (here, in Chapter 1, Item 3), and see there in the Inner Light. And it is explained there that the surrounding light refines the coarseness that is in the screen, until it becomes refined like the screen that is in the Malchut of the Rosh [head]. And in truth all this refining is made at once and in a single moment, as the ARI writes (here, Chapter 1, Item 9); however, since the upper light does not cease from illuminating even for a moment, the upper light is found coupling with it in the four degrees through which the screen passes on its way of refinement, and it brings out there four levels of ten Sefirot, which are Hochma, Bina, ZA, Malchut, as written in the Inner Light (Chapter 1, Item 7).

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:5
items.html:
The completion of the revelation of the vessels is only through the second look
Now the difference between the three kinds of coupling by striking has been explained: for the first look, although it is the root and the source of all the lights and the vessels that are in the Partzuf, nevertheless there is in it no revelation in practice, and the whole revelation is only through the second look, which is made in the degrees of the refinement of the screen; and the matter of this refinement is made by the striking and clash of the inner light and the surrounding light in one another.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, Histaklut Penimit 1:6
items.html:
The last two couplings by striking are for the need of the Partzuf that follows it
And all these three kinds of strikings are for the need of the Partzuf itself; indeed, the matter of the striking and clash of the record with the reflected light in one another is for the need of the vessels of the Partzuf that follows it, as written in the Inner Light (Chapter 2, Item 3). And in this way is the striking of the light of Malchut in the record, which is for the need of the vessel of Malchut of the Partzuf that follows it. Now it has been explained that the first three kinds of strikings are for the need of the Partzuf itself, and the last two strikings are for the need of the Partzuf that follows it.
